notes: Read all 166 source lines before porting. cookieConsent.ts is a non-visual GDPR consent storage helper; only three seams are browser-bound (window.localStorage, the same-document `CustomEvent`, and the cross-tab `storage` event) — everything else is platform-agnostic TypeScript ported 1:1 (contract rules 6 + 7).

L1-24 module doc preserved (the absent-key=unknown contract, side-effect-free design, the CookieConsentBanner/webVitalsReporter/errorReporter subscribers, the never-throw storage-failure philosophy, and the server-side /system/version enforcement re-prompt rationale); a native-conversion section was appended documenting the three native-safe seams.
L26 `export const CONSENT_STORAGE_KEY = 'teslasync:consent:v1'` ported verbatim — the exact storage key and 'accepted'/'declined'/absent contract is unchanged.

L28-36 `export const CONSENT_CHANGED_EVENT = 'cookie-consent-changed'` kept verbatim and still exported for API parity; its doc now notes the same-document CustomEvent is delivered on native via the in-process subscriber registry while cross-surface stays on the native `storage` event.
L38-43 `export type ConsentState = 'unknown' | 'accepted' | 'declined'` ported verbatim with its tri-state doc.

L45-52 the browser-only `safeLocalStorage(): Storage | null` (typeof window guard + window.localStorage in try/catch) is replaced by `safeConsentStorage()` over a structural `ConsentStorage` (getItem/setItem/removeItem) — it prefers a host-injected backend, then an auto-detected global `localStorage` via getGlobalStorage(), else null; never throws. RN's tsconfig omits the DOM `Storage` type so it is modelled structurally (mirrors broadcast.ts's NativeWebStorage).

L54-68 `getConsent()` ported 1:1: null-storage short-circuit returns 'unknown', getItem(CONSENT_STORAGE_KEY) with the raw==='accepted'||'declined' check returning the literal, else 'unknown', and the try/catch fallback to 'unknown' — identical control flow, only safeLocalStorage()->safeConsentStorage().

L70-81 `dispatchChange(state)`: the browser `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(CONSENT_CHANGED_EVENT, {detail: state}))` (same-document only) is replaced by notifying an in-process `listeners` Set — the native analog of the in-tab CustomEvent — with the same per-call try/catch swallow and the same 'next read returns the new value' rationale comment. CustomEvent does not cross documents on the web either, so cross-surface delivery is intentionally NOT done here.

L83-100 `setConsent(state)` ported 1:1: the `if (!ls) { dispatchChange(state); return }` no-storage branch (notify subscribers but do not persist — the exact web fallback), the setItem in try/catch with the silent quota/private-mode comment, and the trailing dispatchChange(state) are all preserved. On react-native-web the setItem auto-fires the native cross-surface `storage` event (no manual dispatch needed).

L102-117 `clearConsent()` ported 1:1: removeItem(CONSENT_STORAGE_KEY) inside `if (ls)` + try/catch silent comment, then unconditional dispatchChange('unknown') so subscribers reset even when storage is absent.

L119-146 `subscribeConsent(cb)`: the web added a same-document `cookie-consent-changed` window listener (onCustom) AND a cross-tab `storage` window listener (onStorage), returning a combined removeEventListener cleanup; the `typeof window === 'undefined'` early `() => undefined` is dropped because the in-process registry works on every platform. Native port: always adds cb to the `listeners` Set (replaces onCustom/the same-document path), and additionally adds an onStorage listener to an auto-detected global `storage` event target (getStorageEventTarget) for cross-surface parity on react-native-web — preserving the original `if (e.key && e.key !== CONSENT_STORAGE_KEY) return; cb(getConsent())` key-filter logic verbatim. The returned unsubscribe is idempotent (an `active` guard) and removes both the Set entry and the storage listener. StorageEvent/EventTarget are typed structurally (NativeStorageEvent/NativeStorageEventTarget) since the DOM lib is unavailable.

L148-166 `isReportingAllowed(requireCookieConsent)` ported verbatim — `if (!requireCookieConsent) return true; return getConsent() === 'accepted'` with its full policy doc (requireCookieConsent=false => always allowed; =true => only after Accept, unknown/declined block).

Browser-only dependency handling (contract rule 7): localStorage + same-document CustomEvent + cross-tab storage event are DOM-only. Added an exported ConsentStorage seam + setConsentStorage() host-injection point + CONSENT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE_REASON explicit no-persistence state — the native analog established by the sibling broadcast.ts port (setBroadcastTransport / BROADCAST_BUS_UNAVAILABLE_REASON). The default auto-detects global localStorage so the react-native-web build keeps full web parity (persistence + cross-surface storage event); pure native is a documented no-persistence state where getConsent returns 'unknown' (the correct GDPR re-prompt behaviour the web already falls back to) while same-runtime subscribers are still notified via the registry.

No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or web UI components imported — no imports at all. Style matches .prettierrc.js (singleQuote, trailingComma all, arrowParens avoid, semicolons).
